content.title: About
content.content: Lettuce is a leafy vegetable commonly used as a fresh topping for sandwiches, salads, and other dishes. It has a crisp texture, mild flavor, and a slightly bitter note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: There are over 100 varieties of lettuce, including romaine, iceberg, butterhead, and leaf lettuce.
Lettuce is composed of more than 95% water, making it an excellent source of hydration.
Lettuce leaves can absorb light but perform photosynthesis less efficiently than many other plants.
Beyond raw consumption, lettuce is sometimes lightly sautéed or steamed in culinary applications.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Lettuce provides a good amount of vitamin K, which is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and folate
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, while folate is important for cell division and fetal development during pregnancy.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Lettuce is very low in calories, making it helpful for weight management.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Leafy greens contain carotenoids and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in lettuce promotes regular bowel movements and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Lettuce can be contaminated with bacteria such as E. coli, so thorough washing before consumption is important.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional lettuce may contain pesticide residues; choosing organic or washing well reduces the risk.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to leafy vegetables, resulting in itching or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lettuce is typically eaten raw: added to sandwiches, salads, wraps, and smoothies. It can also be lightly sautéed, steamed, or incorporated into warm dishes while retaining its crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store lettuce in the refrigerator in an airtight container or bag with a small amount of moisture. Use within 3–5 days. Discard if leaves turn yellow or develop an off odor.
